mainEntity.name: How often should air ducts be cleaned in a Medford home?

acceptedAnswer.text: The general EPA/NADCA recommendation is every 3–5 years for standard homes. For Medford specifically, we recommend every 2–3 years due to wildfire smoke season accumulation, plus cleaning after any significant smoke event, after renovation work, at move-in, or any time you notice a smoke or musty smell when the furnace runs. Homes with pets or documented allergy conditions benefit from the more frequent end of the range.

mainEntity.name: Will air duct cleaning help with wildfire smoke smell?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — if the smoke smell is coming from the duct system, cleaning is the fix. Diagnostic: if the smell is strongest when the HVAC runs, the ducts are the source; if present without the HVAC running and concentrated in specific areas, carpet or other surfaces may be the source. Often both need treatment, and the sequence matters — clean ducts first, then carpet. See our carpet smell guide.

mainEntity.name: Can air duct cleaning help with allergies in Jackson County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — particularly for allergy households in the Rogue Valley's high-pollen spring. Pollen, dust mite allergens, and pet dander that accumulate in ductwork are redistributed by the HVAC continuously; cleaning removes this reservoir. Combined with a fresh MERV-13+ filter and carpet cleaning, duct cleaning is a meaningful allergen-reduction intervention. See our pollen guide.

mainEntity.name: Should I clean the ducts or carpet first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ducts first, then carpet. If you clean the carpet first and then run the HVAC through dirty ducts, the freshly cleaned carpet will be recontaminated within days as the duct system redistributes accumulated material. The correct sequence: ducts → new HVAC filter → carpet.

mainEntity.name: Do you clean air ducts in commercial buildings in Medford?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — commercial HVAC duct cleaning in Medford's office parks, medical facilities, and commercial properties. Commercial systems vary significantly in size and layout; we assess them at a site visit before providing a quote.

mainEntity.name: How long does air duct cleaning take for a typical Medford home?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard 3-bedroom Medford home with a single-zone forced-air system: 3–5 hours. Larger homes, multi-zone systems, or homes with significant contamination (multiple wildfire seasons, renovation dust) take longer. We provide a time estimate at booking, and the home is accessible throughout.
